title: 2208-decentralized-transformers-with-centralized-aggregation-are
universal_lens: MARIE is a sample-efficient multi-agent world model that factorizes the transition kernel into a decentralized per-agent Transformer (φ) predicting local observation tokens and a centralized Perceiver (f θ ) aggregating global context vectors e t i . This separation yields O(n) scaling with agent count n instead of exponential growth, enabling scalable imagination while preserving stationarity through shared global information.
gsi_mapping: MARIE's discrete tokenization and per-agent Transformer predictions map to a Bayesian sequential decision problem where each agent i maintains a posterior over latent states p(s t i |x ≤t i , a ≤t i ) . The centralized Perceiver provides a sufficient statistic for the joint posterior p(S t |X t , A t ) , allowing each agent to condition its policy ψ(a t i |S t i ) on global context while maintaining tractable local inference.
gse_mapping: MARIE implements a distributed state-transition engine where each agent independently samples next token sequences under a shared global context. The Perceiver's role-structured variant enables efficient situational reasoning by decomposing the joint state space into role-mediated interactions, reducing the number of required attention queries.

primitives.name: MARIE Decentralized Transformer
primitives.verbatim_quote: The proposed MARIE (Multi-Agent auto-Regressive Imagination for Efficient learning) combines a shared Transformer local-dynamics model, a VQ-VAE observation tokenizer, a Perceiver agent-wise aggregation module, and discrete reward/discount predictors, training policies purely in imagination.
primitives.assumptions: Fixed agent count n; discrete action spaces; CTDE paradigm; replay buffer used only for world-model training; imagination horizon H assumed constant.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Exponential blow-up of centralised models with n; non-stationarity due to other agents' interventions in fully decentralised settings.

layer2.mapping: MARIE's architecture mirrors the variational free energy minimisation framework of predictive coding, where the Perceiver corresponds to approximate posterior inference over global states, and the Transformers correspond to generative models of local sensory streams. This duality allows MARIE to perform efficient offline planning while maintaining online adaptability.
layer2.telemetry: Reconstruction error on held-out observation tokens; KL divergence between predicted and true action distributions; performance gap between imagination-based policy evaluation and real environment rollouts.

primitives.name: Perceiver Aggregation Module
primitives.verbatim_quote: 5): (e_t^1,...,e_t^n)=f_θ(all agents' tokens+actions) — a Perceiver compressing the n(K+1)-length joint obs-action sequence into n per-agent global-context vectors (each agent's "view" of the global situation).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: e_t^i : per-agent global context vector ∈ R^{n_e}; f_θ : Perceiver function; all agents' tokens and actions : joint sequence of length n(K+1); n : number of agents; K : number of token types per agent.
primitives.assumptions: Global context vectors are informative summaries of the joint history; the Perceiver's compression ratio is sufficient to retain relevant inter-agent dependencies.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when the compressed representation loses critical information about agent interactions, leading to suboptimal joint behaviour.

layer2.mapping: The Perceiver's cross-attention mechanism implements a soft differentiable memory access pattern, retrieving relevant past experiences from a large dataset. This is analogous to a key-value store in classical reinforcement learning, where keys are query patterns and values are stored trajectories.
layer2.telemetry: Number of unique attention heads; average attention sparsity; reconstruction accuracy of the original joint sequence from the aggregated context vectors.

reasoning_traces.think:
MARIE addresses the multi-agent exploration-exploitation dilemma by separating dynamics into local and global components. The local Transformers φ capture agent-specific stochasticity, while the Perceiver f θ provides a deterministic summary of the joint state. This factorization reduces the variance in policy gradient estimates, accelerating convergence. However, the assumption of Markovian independence given the global context may fail in games with long-term co-ordination requirements, necessitating longer imagination horizons or hierarchical extensions.
